crops.bengaluru_season_note: Best Oct-Feb. Grows year-round with 35-50% shade (ZipGrow range 7-29 °C, ideal 18 °C), but Mar-May heat gives tough, bitter leaves, aphids and whitefly, and Jun-Oct cloud slows regrowth. Does not bolt in the first year.
crops.demand_note: Steady state 44 g/site/40 d (16-79). Revenue per site per 40 d: Rs 4.0 wholesale, Rs 6.6 HoReCa, Rs 19.8 retail. Rank 5/12. Hyperpure sells curly kale to restaurants at Rs 144/kg, so wholesale and HoReCa do not cover the fixed costs. Retail demand is steady but modest: BigBasket hydroponic 100-125 g Rs 52-60; OnlyHydroponics BLR Rs 75/100 g; Healthy Buddha organic Rs 59/100 g.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Same as curly kale: best Oct-Feb; needs shade in Mar-May. The upright strap leaves suit towers.
crops.demand_note: 44 g/site/40 d. Rs 5.3 / 8.8 / 26.3 per site per 40 d. Rank 4 at HoReCa and rank 1 at retail. Not listed on Hyperpure or BigBasket. OnlyHydroponics BLR sells 100 g Rs 99 and 500 g Rs 349. The HoReCa price is an estimate. The market is very small (Italian restaurants, salad bars). Seed costs about Rs 4 per seed (Cavolo Nero 100 seeds Rs 400).

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Most heat-tolerant of the temperate greens here. It is a biennial, so it does not bolt in the first year (ZipGrow range 13-24 °C). Best Oct-Feb; use shade in Mar-May. The monsoon brings Cercospora leaf spot and leaf miner.
crops.demand_note: 63 g/site/40 d (24-105). Rs 6.3 / 10.0 / 22.0 per site per 40 d. Rank 1 at HoReCa. Not on Hyperpure, so the HoReCa price is an estimate (25% below Trikaya's Rs 220/kg retail). Hydroponic chard was out of stock at OnlyHydroponics BLR (Rs 99/100 g) and BigBasket (130 g Rs 167). Demand is niche.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Best Oct-Feb (ZipGrow range 13-24 °C). In Mar-May, bolting, bitterness and tipburn increase, so use heat-tolerant hybrids and shade. Flea beetle, diamondback moth and aphids occur all year. Cold-night bolting (<10 °C) is not a risk here.
crops.demand_note: 64 g/site/40 d (25-127). Rs 5.1 / 9.0 / 22.4 per site per 40 d. Rank 3. The fastest good-value crop: first sale about 48 days after sowing. Hyperpure bok choy costs Rs 136/kg. BigBasket pak choi 250 g Rs 39; Trikaya baby 250 g Rs 75; BigBasket hydroponic head Rs 115. Asian and Indo-Chinese restaurants give steady demand. When all 90 sites are planted, heads stay about 60 g (baby); plant alternate sites for 100-150 g heads.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Only Nov-Feb without a chiller. Cornell: keep the solution at 15-20 °C (never above 25 °C) and DO at 4 ppm or more. Do not re-cut, or Pythium builds up and kills the crop. Unchilled Bengaluru towers run warmer for most of the year, and the plants also bolt in heat.
crops.demand_note: 38 g/site/40 d (12-88). Rs 4.9 / 9.4 / 18.8 per site per 40 d. It ranks 2nd on paper, but only for about 4 months and with 30-50% losses. Baby spinach retails at Rs 59-99/100 g (BigBasket, Trikaya, OnlyHydroponics). Hyperpure lists only palak (Rs 62/kg), so restaurants use palak instead. The HoReCa price is an estimate.

crops.crop: Palak (Indian spinach, Beta vulgaris var. bengalensis)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Grows year-round and tolerates heat better than English spinach. Growth is slower, with more leaf spot, in the heavy monsoon (Aug-Oct).
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY. The agronomic fit is good but the economics are poor. 47 g/site/40 d; Rs 0.9 / 2.8 / 4.7 per site per 40 d; rank 12 (last). Farmers' markets pay Rs 20-22/kg (Agmarknet, Sep 2026), and Hyperpure delivers palak at Rs 62/kg. BigBasket cleaned palak sells at Rs 28-40/kg in 100-500 g packs. Bunching labour (about Rs 39/kg, estimate) is higher than the field price. Mass demand, but fields supply it cheaply (TNAU: 20 t/ha in 3 months).

crops.crop: Red amaranth (lal math / red harive-dantu soppu)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Warm-season C4 crop, sown all year (TNAU). Best Mar-Oct and tolerates the Bengaluru summer. It may slow and flower early in the cool Nov-Jan days (estimate). Caterpillars and leaf webbers are pests; wet rot and white rust increase in the monsoon.
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY at scale. 62 g/site/40 d; Rs 1.7 / 5.6 / 7.4 per site per 40 d; rank 7. Farmers' markets pay Rs 25-35/kg (Krishnagiri, Denkanikottai, Sep 2026); Hyperpure Rs 92/kg. BigBasket: cleaned 250 g Rs 34; with roots 500 g Rs 17.6; hydroponic 100 g Rs 71 (tiny niche). Fastest multi-cut crop (first cut 32 days after sowing).

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Same as red amaranth: best Mar-Oct; more wet rot in the monsoon.
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY at scale. 64 g/site/40 d; Rs 1.7 / 6.1 / 7.7 per site per 40 d; rank 6. Hyperpure green amaranth 250 g Rs 25 (Rs 100/kg). BigBasket cleaned 250 g Rs 32; with roots 500 g Rs 22; Organic Mandya bunch Rs 46-48. Field supply is Rs 25-35/kg.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Best Oct-Feb (cool and dry). The monsoon brings damping-off, root rot and mildew, but prices rise. Summer growing is possible with shade. Sow 10-15 seeds directly in each plug.
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY. 33 g/site/40 d; Rs 1.0 / 3.3 / 3.3 per site per 40 d; rank 10. Farmers' markets pay about Rs 30/kg (Agmarknet median, Sep 2026). Hyperpure's Rs 116/kg is a monsoon price. BigBasket cleaned methi sells at Rs 46-107/kg. It is the fastest crop (first sale about 25 days after sowing), but it gives the lowest grams per site.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Grows year-round. Thrips are a problem in the dry Mar-May period; purple blotch and Stemphylium appear in the monsoon. Scallions grow on towers, but bulb onions do not (Agrotonomy).
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY. 33 g/site/40 d; Rs 1.5 / 2.9 / 3.3 per site per 40 d; rank 11. Bengaluru wholesale was about Rs 44/kg (29 Sep 2026); Krishnagiri farmers' markets pay Rs 85-110/kg in the monsoon; Hyperpure Rs 92/kg; BigBasket Rs 42-47/kg. Indo-Chinese restaurants create large demand, but the crop is slow (about 70 days from seed to first cut) and gives few grams per site.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Needs cool weather to form heads: Oct-Jan only. Heat causes tipburn, soft rot and bolting. Heads are heavy, and a field crop needs 45x45 cm spacing (TNAU), so a 90-site tower can carry only mini heads on alternate sites.
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY. 56 g/site/40 d; Rs 2.3 / 5.1 / 6.8 per site per 40 d; rank 8. Fields from cooler districts supply it cheaply: regular cabbage was Rs 15-19/kg at Binny Mill APMC (Sep 2026); Hyperpure sells Chinese cabbage at Rs 84 per piece; BigBasket head (750 g-1 kg) Rs 94. The hydroponic mini head (Rs 171 for 200-300 g) is a tiny niche. Johnny's gives 45-64 days to maturity.

crops.bengaluru_season_note: Cool-season crop (ZipGrow range 10-24 °C): grow Oct-Feb only. It bolts quickly in the Mar-May heat. Aphids are severe; cabbage loopers and flea beetles also attack.
crops.demand_note: LOSES MONEY. 46 g/site/40 d; Rs 0.9 / 3.7 / 5.5 per site per 40 d; rank 9. Hyperpure Rs 84/kg; BigBasket 250 g Rs 22 and bunch 180-200 g Rs 24; Healthy Buddha organic 200 g Rs 49 (out of stock). Bengaluru demand is small and mostly in winter (North Indian sarson saag).

risks: Hyperpure already supplies Bengaluru restaurants at Rs 144/kg for curly kale, Rs 136/kg for bok choy, Rs 62/kg for palak and Rs 84-116/kg for other Indian greens (29 Sep 2026). Tower produce must match these prices.
A 90-site tower is dense, so each site gets little light and the grams per site stay low. Published tower trials show 23-42% less kale and 31% less lettuce per plant than flat systems.
Unchilled nutrient solution gets warm in March-May. Spinach gets Pythium root rot. Pak choi, mustard and Chinese cabbage bolt, turn bitter or get tipburn.
June-October brings cloud and high humidity. Growth slows, and leaf-spot, mildew and wet-rot losses increase, mainly in methi, amaranth, chard and brassicas.
Diamondback moth, aphids and flea beetles attack brassicas. Leaf miners attack chard and spinach, and thrips attack spring onion. A pesticide-free claim limits the spray options.
Leaf picking and bunching are slow. Estimated harvest labour of Rs 31-75/kg is more than the Rs 15-45/kg field price of palak, methi, amaranth and mustard.

One crop on all 54,000 sites gives 44-87 kg per day. On 29 Sep 2026, hydroponic chard and bok choy were out of stock at Bengaluru sellers, which suggests thin retail demand. Unsold greens spoil in a few days.

Floruvi list prices are 1.4 times the benchmark. For example, bok choy is Rs 208.60 per 250 g, against Rs 99 per 250 g at OnlyHydroponics Bengaluru and Rs 136/kg at Hyperpure. Sales volume at list price will be low.
In the first 2-3 cycles, a semi-experienced grower can lose 20-50% of the plants. The yields in this study are estimates, and only a pilot can confirm them.
Many hybrid seeds (Darkibor kale, Cavolo Nero, Choko pak choi) were listed as out of stock. Seed supply can delay planting.
600 towers at Rs 5,000-12,000 each cost Rs 30-72 lakh. This is more than the Rs 20 lakh capital, before the polyhouse, pumps and working capital.
recommendations: Do not grow palak, methi, amaranth, mustard, spring onion or Chinese cabbage in towers for sale. If Floruvi boxes need them, buy them from nearby farms.
Test pak choi, Swiss chard and curly kale first in 20-30 towers for 2-3 cycles. Measure the grams per site per 40 days before you buy more towers.
Sell exotic greens mainly through Floruvi boxes and direct retail at Rs 350-600/kg. Send only surplus to restaurants, at or near Hyperpure prices.
Before you plant each batch, get written weekly orders from restaurants or box customers. Sow small batches every week.
Grow English/baby spinach only from November to February. At other times, grow it only with a chiller that keeps the solution at 20-25 °C or less.
If buyers want 100-150 g pak choi heads, plant only alternate sites.
In March-May, use 35-50% shade, white or insulated reservoirs and root-zone cooling. Keep dissolved oxygen above 4 ppm.
Use 40-mesh insect net, yellow and blue sticky traps and Bt against caterpillars. Check the crop every week, and remove leaves with leaf miners at once.
For cash within 3 months, sow pak choi and chard in October. The first sales come about 48 days after sowing.

Every week, record the harvest weight, losses and labour hours for each tower. Stop any crop that earns less than its labour and fixed-cost share (about Rs 2.44 per site per 40 days for each Rs 1 lakh of monthly overhead).
sources: Mattson N.S. & Peters C., 'A Recipe for Hydroponic Success' (Cornell) - local research copy, URL not verified

topic: Strawberries in vertical towers and microgreens as a quick-cash line for Floruvi, Bengaluru (2026 data, INR)
summary: Microgreens are the only option here that can bring in cash within 30 days. Radish, pea and sunflower are ready 9-12 days after sowing, so sales can start around day 15, but the first month earns only about Rs 15,600 at 50 trays a week. Bengaluru shops sell microgreens at Rs 79-149 per 50 g, Rs 149-179 per 100 g and Rs 130 per live tray (Trikaya, NayaGreens, Nutriofarms, BigBasket). Floruvi's current Rs 280 per 50 g and Rs 182 per tray are well above that. Base case (Rs 1,000/kg blended price, 208 g sold per tray, 10% loss): monthly cash profit is about Rs 11,000 at 50 trays a week, Rs 24,500 at 100 and Rs 51,500 at 200. That is Rs 14,500, Rs 32,000 and Rs 68,000 per 40 days. Rack setups need about Rs 1.6, 2.7 and 5.2 lakh. The break-even price is about Rs 700/kg. If yields or prices slip, the business loses Rs 14,000-50,000 a month, and small hobby seed packs alone cost about Rs 145 per tray. Strawberries in towers are weak: base 150 g marketable fruit per plant per season (low 60 g from a 2025 US tower trial, high 330 g from Karnataka polyhouse trials). They are planted Oct-Nov, fruit Dec-Apr and must be replanted every year. Averaged over a year, one strawberry site earns about Rs 4.9 and uses about Rs 3.0 of consumables per 40 days. Bengaluru can probably absorb 10-25 kg of microgreens a week from a new seller within 3 months (estimate), which is about 50-120 trays a week.

crops.crop: Strawberry (short-day Winter Dawn, Nabila, Sweet Charlie; day-neutral Monterey or Albion only from licensed plants)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Plant 15 Oct-15 Nov, after the heaviest rain (Sep-Oct). First fruit comes in Dec. Pick every 2-3 days until Mar/Apr (about 120 days, about 40 picks). Heat above about 33 C in Mar-May and humidity from Jun to Nov end the season, so replant every year. Grams per harvest = season total (60/150/330 g per plant) divided by 40 picks. Averaged over 365 days this is about 16 g sellable per site per 40 days (base). One cycle equals one year. The loss rates cover spoilage and unsold fruit (shelf life is 2-4 days).
crops.demand_note: Bengaluru buys strawberries mainly Dec-Mar. Supply comes from Mahabaleshwar and Ooty/Kodaikanal. BigBasket lists 200 g at Rs 43-187. OnlyHydroponics lists hydroponic 200 g at Rs 159 (out of stock in Sep). Fruit from a 5-10 tower pilot sells easily through D2C and cafes. All 600 towers (about 8 t per season) would push the price down to wholesale (Rs 150-180/kg).

crops.crop: Radish microgreens (rack trays, not towers; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Can be grown all year indoors. Use 2-3 days of blackout, then light. Humidity from Jun to Nov raises the risk of damping-off, so run fans and sanitise seed. The research yield is 2,259 g/m2 at 10 days (271 g per tray).
crops.demand_note: The best-selling microgreen. Bengaluru prices: Trikaya Rs 79/50 g, BigBasket Rs 88.77/50 g, NayaGreens Rs 99/60 g and Rs 149/100 g, Nutriofarms Rs 149/50 g. Wholesale and HoReCa prices are estimates. Consumables = 25 g seed Rs 15 + cocopeat Rs 12 + packs Rs 10 + power Rs 5 + sanitation Rs 2.

crops.crop: Pea shoots (rack trays; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Soak the seed 8-12 h. Grows all year. Handles Mar-May heat better than brassicas. The research yield is about 2,800 g/m2 at 10 days (about 336 g per tray).
crops.demand_note: Heavy per tray, and chefs and salad buyers like it. Bengaluru prices: NayaGreens Rs 110/60 g and Rs 179/100 g, Trikaya Rs 79/50 g. Seed is the main cost (200 g at Rs 350/kg = Rs 70). Food-grade peas (Rs 104-119/kg) cut this cost if they germinate well.

crops.crop: Sunflower shoots (rack trays; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Soak the seed 8-12 h. Hulls must be removed at harvest, which adds labour. Research yields are 1,657-3,510 g/m2 at 9-10 days.
crops.demand_note: Bengaluru prices: NayaGreens Rs 99/60 g and Rs 149/100 g, Trikaya Rs 79/50 g, BigBasket Rs 50/20 g. Bulk seed costs Rs 280/kg on Tradeindia (MOQ 150 kg) against Rs 2,680/kg in hobby packs. Base uses 100 g seed at Rs 450/kg.

crops.crop: Broccoli microgreens (rack trays; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Grows all year indoors. Sensitive to damping-off when humid. The research yield is 1,461 g/m2 at 11 days (175 g per tray).
crops.demand_note: Buyers see it as a health product. Bengaluru prices: NayaGreens Rs 179/100 g, Nutriofarms Rs 179/50 g, Trikaya Rs 50/25 g. Seed decides whether it pays: 15 g at an estimated bulk Rs 6,000/kg = Rs 90 per tray, and at the hobby price of Rs 19,900/kg the seed alone costs Rs 300 per tray. Grow it only with bulk seed.

crops.crop: Mustard microgreens (rack trays; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Grows all year and fast. The research yield is 1,082 g/m2 at 12 days (130 g per tray).
crops.demand_note: Spicy flavour suits Indian and fusion dishes. Bengaluru prices: Trikaya Rs 79/50 g, NayaGreens Rs 99/60 g and Rs 149/100 g, Nutriofarms Rs 149/50 g. Seed is cheap (12 g). Food-grade rai costs Rs 105/kg on BigBasket; test germination first.

crops.crop: Red amaranth microgreens (rack trays; site = one 10x20 inch tray)
crops.bengaluru_season_note: Slow and small. Easily damaged by overwatering and by humidity from Jun to Nov. The research yield is 897 g/m2 at 18 days (108 g per tray).
crops.demand_note: Chefs value it for colour. Bengaluru prices: Trikaya Rs 150/50 g, NayaGreens Rs 179/100 g, Nutriofarms Rs 149/50 g. Seed costs Rs 750-2,760/kg (Desikheti, Ugaoo, Organic Bazar) but only 8 g per tray. Low yield keeps it a small share of the mix.

risks: Strawberry pollination: in a 2025 University of Georgia trial, tower plants gave at most about 60 g of marketable fruit each, mainly because pollination was poor. Bees raised yields by 40-50% in other trials.
Strawberry climate: Bengaluru reaches 33-35 C in Mar-May, which ends fruiting. Humidity is 75-81% from Jun to Nov, which brings grey mould and leaf spot. Plants must be replaced every year.

Strawberry market: fruit keeps only 2-4 days at room temperature. Prices fall when Mahabaleshwar supply peaks (Jan-Mar). Volume from 600 towers would sell only at wholesale prices of about Rs 150-180/kg.

Strawberry economics: base revenue is about Rs 4.9 per site per 40 days, against Rs 3.0 of consumables, before picking labour and power. With 90 sites per tower, the lower pockets get shade and yield less.
Microgreen price: BigBasket (Rs 36-89 per pack) and existing sellers (NayaGreens, Nutriofarms, Trikaya) set what buyers expect to pay. Below about Rs 700/kg blended, every volume level loses money.
Microgreen sell-through: the product is perishable (about 5-10 days chilled). Unsold stock and failed trays in the first cycles can take 25% of output.
Seed risk: hobby packs make seed cost about Rs 145 per tray. Fungicide-treated field seed is unsafe for microgreens. Food-grade seed may germinate poorly.
Food safety and compliance: microgreens need clean seed, sanitation, cold chain and FSSAI registration. Ask a CA to confirm the GST treatment.

Channel readiness: payments on the Floruvi site are still disabled, so D2C orders need UPI or WhatsApp until Razorpay is switched on. Quick-commerce listings need GST and FSSAI, and they take a margin.
Cash pressure: base microgreen profit covers the Rs 40,000/month commitment only at about 150-200 trays a week, and that requires about 30-37 kg of sales a week.
recommendations: Start microgreens now at 50 trays a week on a 100-tray rack setup (about Rs 0.8-1.6 lakh). Grow radish, pea, sunflower and mustard first.
Buy untreated seed in 1-25 kg lots and test germination on 2 trays first. Do not buy 25-50 g hobby packs. Add broccoli only after you find bulk seed at Rs 6,000/kg or less.

Get buyers before you grow more: sample 20 cafes and restaurants in weeks 1-2 and sign 10. Scale up to 100 trays and then 200 trays a week only when weekly sales reach about 20 kg and then about 37 kg.

Proposal for the owner: set Bengaluru microgreen prices close to the local market (50 g Rs 79-99, 100 g Rs 149-179, live tray Rs 130-150). Current Floruvi prices (Rs 280 per 50 g) are 2-3.5 times the local price.
Sell live mini-trays (cost about Rs 22 each) through D2C for early cash from day 7-10. Take orders by UPI or WhatsApp until site payments are active.
Track yield per tray, loss and realised Rs/kg every week. Stop scaling if the blended price stays below Rs 700/kg for 4 weeks.

Do not put the 600 towers into strawberries. At most, run a 5-10 tower pilot (450-900 Winter Dawn or Nabila plants at Rs 10-15 each). Plant 15 Oct-15 Nov 2026 under insect netting, with bee boxes or hand pollination.
Measure marketable grams per plant and the price you get in the strawberry pilot until Apr 2027. Scale up only if the pilot beats 250 g per plant and Rs 300/kg.
Register with FSSAI, put the harvest date on every pack, keep packs at 2-4 C, and deliver within 48 hours of harvest.

topic: Bengaluru produce price sheet by sales channel (2025–2026): wholesale/aggregator, HoReCa, modern retail/quick commerce, direct-to-consumer
summary: On 29 Sep 2026, Hyperpure (Zomato's restaurant supplier) charged Bengaluru restaurants ₹140–216/kg for loose-leaf, romaine and lollo rosso lettuce. It charged ₹99/kg for iceberg, ₹236/kg for arugula, ₹150/kg for basil and curly parsley, ₹136/kg for bok choy and celery, and ₹62–80/kg for palak, coriander and mint. Traders near Bengaluru and in Ooty ask ₹35–65/kg for soil-grown lettuce, and a Karnataka hydroponic farm (Bidar) asks ₹90–120/kg for lollo rosso, green lettuce and Thai basil. From these, plan on about ₹40–130/kg farm-gate for leafy crops (estimate). BigBasket, which also runs BB Now quick commerce, sells hydroponic live-root lettuce heads at ₹61–85 per 125–200 g (about ₹375–525/kg), hydroponic basil at ₹620/kg, microgreens at ₹1,600–2,500/kg and strawberries at ₹215–342/kg. I found no public crop-level retailer margin; at an assumed 30% margin (range 25–40%), a supplier gets about ₹280/kg for a hydroponic lettuce head, before 5–20% rejections. Floruvi's current site prices are 1.4–8.6 times Bengaluru shelf prices (iceberg ₹1,120/kg against ₹130/kg), so they cannot sell tower-scale volumes. Restaurants expect credit (Hyperpure offers pay-later lines), BigBasket says it pays farmers within 48 hours, and 86% of B2B produce sellers on TradeIndia offer advance payment, while only 3% offer credit. Zepto, Blinkit and Instamart blocked automated reading, and the web-search budget was already used up, so BigBasket stands in for quick commerce and I read every source directly.

risks: Data gaps: Zepto, Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart blocked automated reading with bot checks, and I did not try to get around them. IndiaMART returned rate limits (HTTP 429), the HOPCOMS site did not resolve, Namdhari's Fresh loads only by script, and Agmarknet has no Bengaluru data for exotic crops. The web-search budget was already used up, so all sources were read directly. BigBasket (which runs BB Now) stands in for quick commerce.
All prices are a one-day snapshot (29 Sep 2026, monsoon, strawberry off-season). Fresh-produce prices move daily. Several listings were out of stock and may show old prices.

Competition: BigBasket already lists 24 hydroponic lettuce SKUs in Bengaluru (20 in stock) at ₹47–85 per head, and Hyperpure sells soil lettuce to restaurants at ₹140–216/kg. A new farm must win on quality and reliability, not on price.
Price gap: Floruvi's list prices (₹350–1,493/kg for lettuce) are 1.4–8.6× local shelf prices. A revenue model built on them will overstate income.
Commodity herbs (coriander, mint, palak) sell at ₹62–80/kg to restaurants and ₹36–45/kg in bulk. They cannot pay for tower sites.

Credit and rejection: restaurants expect credit (Hyperpure offers pay-later lines), and retailers reject at inward QC and accept doorstep returns. Slow payment plus 5–20% shrink can strain cash while ₹40,000/month is also due.

Volume against channel size: 54,000 sites can yield roughly 100+ kg of greens a day (shared lettuce model, estimate). A restaurant buys about 0.25–2 kg per item per order (estimate), so dozens of accounts or a distributor contract are needed before full planting.
Farm-gate and HoReCa values for butterhead, oakleaf, Swiss chard, English spinach, Thai basil, microgreens and strawberries rest on few data points, data from outside Bengaluru, or estimates.

City attribution: BigBasket's city comes from its default cookie (city id 1, treated as Bengaluru), and Nature's Basket does not show its default store's city. Delhi B2B asks are higher than Bengaluru prices and must not be used as local farm-gate prices.
recommendations: Sell most tower output to HoReCa at or just under Hyperpure prices: lettuce ₹140–216/kg, arugula ₹236/kg, basil and parsley ₹150/kg. Ask 20–60% more only for visibly better hydroponic product (live-root heads, clean leaves, longer shelf life); Hyperpure's own hydroponic SKUs carry that premium.

Choose tower crops where the Bengaluru HoReCa price is at least ₹150/kg and tower fit is good: lollo rosso, oakleaf, butterhead (live-root heads), arugula, Italian and Thai basil, curly kale and pak choi. Do not grow coriander, mint, palak, iceberg or celery in towers.
Reprice the Floruvi site to Bengaluru prices before launch. Test ₹60–90 per live-root head and ₹60–75 per 100 g basil against OnlyHydroponics BLR (₹59–75) and BigBasket (₹61–85 per head).
Use D2C (Floruvi site, apartment groups, weekend markets) for premium packs and boxes, but plan it as a small share of volume. D2C orders are 0.2–1 kg and carry ₹40–99 delivery each (estimate).
Enter quick commerce and modern retail only after FSSAI, GSTIN, a trademark filing and barcodes are in place. Model the supplier price at 0.60–0.75 × shelf price and allow for 5–20% rejections.
Protect cash (proposal): take advance or cash on delivery from new small buyers. Give 7–15 days credit only to vetted accounts. Invoice weekly. Stop supply after 2 unpaid invoices.

Owner action each week: record Hyperpure and BigBasket prices for the 10 target SKUs. Ask 3 KR Market or Singena Agrahara traders and 2 aggregators (for example Hyperpure's vendor team and Ninjacart) for written buy prices. I did not contact anyone.

topic: Bengaluru demand, competition and sales ramp for a 600-tower hydroponic farm (Floruvi), checked 29 Sep 2026
summary: Bengaluru buyers already get exotic greens cheaply. Hyperpure delivers lettuce at ₹99–192/kg (a "hydroponic" line costs ₹264/kg), basil at ₹150/kg and kale at ₹140/kg. Nearby farms ask ₹35–70/kg for bulk lettuce. With one owner-salesperson, a new grower can sell about 26 kg/week at the target price in month 1, 95 kg/week in month 3, 210 kg/week in month 6 and 400 kg/week in month 12. This is the base case: about 3, 10, 22 and 40 business accounts plus 25–300 weekly boxes. 600 towers (54,000 sites, about 1,300 plants a day) would harvest about 1,275 kg/week. Only about 7% of that sells at the target price in month 3, 16% in month 6 and 31% in month 12. The rest (about 90% in month 3, falling to about 50% by month 12) sells at ₹20–50/kg or is wasted. 150 towers (about 320 kg/week) reach about 85% sold at the target price by month 8 (base case). Well-funded competitors lost money. Deep Rooted of Bengaluru (100 acres of greenhouses, 120+ restaurants, 1.25 lakh customers) shut in March 2025 after losing ₹52 crore on ₹34 crore of revenue in FY24. Clover, Otipy and WayCool each lost 55–74% of their revenue. Trading exotic produce from partner farms can start in about 2 weeks at a 12–35% gross margin. In the base case it gives only about ₹30,000 a month of gross profit by December 2026. Recommendation: start with 60–150 towers, sign buyers before planting, price near Hyperpure, and add towers only after 4 weeks at 70% or more sold at the target price.

risks: Oversupply: 600 towers give about 1,275 kg/week. Base-case demand at the target price is only 95 kg/week in month 3, 210 in month 6 and 400 in month 12. About 90% of the harvest in month 3, and about 50% in month 12, would be dumped at ₹20–50/kg or wasted.

Price crash: nearby farms ask ₹35–70/kg for bulk lettuce, and Hyperpure delivers field lettuce at ₹99–192/kg. Pushing large volumes will remove the hydroponic premium (₹264/kg hydroponic against ₹140/kg field leaf lettuce).

Strong competitors already supply the city: Hyperpure (1 lakh+ partners), BigBasket's fresho! hydroponic range, Simply Fresh (Telangana), Trikaya (305 acres, including Ooty), OnlyHydroponics (60,000+ customers), and 147 exotic-vegetable listings from Bengaluru sellers.

Better-funded companies failed. Deep Rooted (Bengaluru; 100 acres of greenhouses, 120+ restaurants) shut in March 2025 after losing ₹52.21 crore on ₹34.37 crore of revenue in FY24. Clover, Otipy and WayCool each lost 55–74% of their revenue.
Home delivery is expensive: Otipy spent about ₹40 to deliver an order worth ₹270. Floruvi's list prices are 40–60% above BigBasket and OnlyHydroponics, so few home buyers will convert.
Credit risk: hotels and chains pay in 30–60 days (estimate). Greenikk shut after ₹6 crore of defaults and needed 6 months to collect 80% of what it was owed.
Quality: a grower with only trial experience will have uneven harvests in the first cycles. One bad week can lose a chef's account (assessment).

Timing: towers planted in October give their first harvest in about December. That leaves about one month of sales before the end-December profit target, in the season when field lettuce is plentiful (assessment).
Owner time: one person cannot grow, sell, deliver and collect payment for 54,000 sites.
Export will not help in the first months. It needs an IEC, APEDA RCMC, an FSSAI Central licence and a phytosanitary certificate for each shipment (repo docs/22).
recommendations: Size the farm to demand. Start with 60–150 towers (about 130–320 kg/week), not 600. Add 50 towers only after 4 weeks in a row with at least 70% of the harvest sold at the target price.
Sign buyers before planting. Before the first harvest, get 10–15 cafés and restaurants to agree to standing weekly orders. Use free samples and 2–3 deliveries a week.

Price near Bengaluru business prices: lettuce ₹150–200/kg delivered, basil ₹160–220, kale ₹150–200, rocket ₹200–250. Do not add the 40% retail markup to business prices. Review Floruvi's home-buyer prices.

Start trading now, within weeks 1–2. Buy from partner growers in Krishnagiri (Hosur), Chittoor, Ooty and Bengaluru. Sell a full basket of exotic produce at a 15–25% gross margin. Give at most one week of credit, and ask new accounts to pay in advance by UPI.

Apply early to channels that buy in bulk, such as Hyperpure (as a supplier), FirstClub, BigBasket and the quick-delivery apps. Get your GSTIN, FSSAI and barcodes first. These channels can take surplus at about ₹90–130/kg.

Plant the crop mix that buyers want: about 60% mixed lettuces, 10–15% basil, 10% kale, and 15–20% rocket, pak choi and herbs. Do not grow iceberg or palak in towers. Keep selling the live microgreen trays to home buyers.
Plant weekly batches that match confirmed orders. Arrange a buyer for surplus before harvest. Measure sell-through, waste and unpaid bills every week.

Learn from the case studies. Rise Hydroponics (₹5 crore revenue) and Barton Breeze earn much of their money from setups and training. Greenu took about 3 years to reach ₹12 lakh a month. Keep spending low, and do not spend heavily on home delivery.

topic: Packaging, cold chain, delivery and channel onboarding for the Floruvi tower farm, Bengaluru (checked 29 September 2026)
summary: Delivery costs more than packaging for a farm on the edge of Bengaluru. Borzo's Bengaluru bike tariff is ₹9/km, plus ₹36 for the first point and ₹13.50 for each extra drop. At that rate, one drop from the farm to the city costs ₹170-400, and a 12-15-drop loop costs about ₹55-85 per drop. An own petrol two-wheeler with a ₹24,000 rider costs about ₹33,000 a month. That is ₹51-127 per drop at 25 to 10 drops a day, so the site's ₹99 delivery fee works only when orders are batched into routes. For restaurants and hotels (HoReCa), an EV three-wheeler (Treo Zor, ₹3.55-3.94 lakh, EMI ₹6,864) delivers at ₹6-28/kg at 250 to 50 kg a day. A Porter three-wheeler starts at ₹205 a trip. Packaging costs ₹2-8/kg for bulk in crates, ₹15-20/kg in 100-250 g pouches or punnets, and about ₹59/kg in 125 g clamshells. A walk-in cold room of 8×8×8 ft costs about ₹1.8-3.8 lakh, and power adds ₹1,700-6,600 a month (BESCOM LT-5, ₹4.40/kWh). A chest freezer that can run as a cooler (₹12-35k) is enough for trials. Registrations cost little: Udyam and GST are free, FSSAI is ₹100 a year, a trademark is ₹4,500 and GS1 barcodes are ₹50,200 in year 1. Quick commerce also needs e-invoicing and weeks of lead time, so Hyperpure (refundable fee, 3-5 business-day review, GSTIN optional) and direct HoReCa are the realistic first B2B channels. Wastage estimates are 2-10% on own channels and 3-15% on platforms. Conventional Indian vegetable chains lose 4.8-11.6% after harvest.

line_items.source: Hyperpure Seller Hub app text (https://seller.hyperpure.com/), read 29 September 2026
line_items.note: The onboarding fee is 100% refundable (amount not shown). GSTIN is optional ('type NA if not registered'). The form has an Udyam field. Buying is through bids and purchase orders. The bid price is final. QC failures are rejected, and delays or shortfalls get penalties. Approved packaging and FSSAI compliance are required. Payment comes after delivery and GRN, on a credit period set at onboarding.

line_items.name: Quick-commerce onboarding (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart)
line_items.source: docs/22-growth-channels-research.md, checked 27 September 2026: https://seller.blinkit.com/faq, https://seller.blinkit.com/fees-commission, https://brands.zepto.co.in/, https://www.swiggy.com/instamart-partner. Blinkit pages returned HTTP 403 on 29 September
line_items.note: Needs GSTIN, PAN, bank proof, a trademark certificate or application (or brand NOC), FSSAI and GS1/UPC barcodes. Blinkit also needs IRN e-invoicing and a digital signature (DSC). Blinkit charges no registration fee. It charges product-ID activation, inwarding, storage and fulfilment fees and a commission; the rates are behind login. Zepto takes up to 15 business days after selection. Base assumes about 4 weeks to get the documents (estimate).

line_items.source: Estimate: platforms do not publish fresh-produce margins. The range allows for platform gross margin and wastage
line_items.note: BigBasket buys direct from 50,000+ farmers through 120+ collection centres (press release cited in docs/22). Namdhari's Fresh has no public supplier page (its site is JS-only; not verified). Model modern retail at 55-70% (estimate).

line_items.name: Days from delivery to cash (B2B mix)
line_items.source: BigBasket pays farmers within 48 h of goods receipt (press release via docs/22: https://www.apnnews.com/on-kisan-diwas-bigbasket-reaches-milestone-of-50000-registered-farmers-in-its-direct-sourcing-network/). Hyperpure: agreed credit period, not public. HoReCa 7-30 days and quick commerce 30-45 days are estimates
line_items.note: Own prepaid B2C orders settle in about 1-3 days (estimate).

line_items.source: FoSCoS kind-of-business eligibility, updated 1 April 2026 (https://foscos.fssai.gov.in/assets/docs/Revised_2ndApril2026KindofBusinessEligibility.pdf). FSSAI order of 13 March 2026 on turnover thresholds (https://www.fssai.gov.in/upload/advisories/2026/03/69b4054bb6cd6Order%20dated%2013thMarch2026_Revised%20Turnover%20threshold.pdf)

Central licence ₹7,500, which 'E-Commerce' and 'Trader/Merchant - Exporter' also need at any turnover. The 2026 amendment gives perpetual validity. line_items.source: Udyam portal: 'Registration Process is totally free' (https://udyamregistration.gov.in/). The government charges no GST registration fee

line_items.source: Estimate for insulated city runs of 3 h or less. Shelf-life data in docs/28: mustard microgreens last 14 days at 5 °C and 1 day at 20 °C (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9966302/)

line_items.source: Estimate. Hyperpure terms: QC deviations are rejected, and weight must match the PO within tolerance (Seller Hub text)

line_items.name: Benchmark: conventional vegetable post-harvest loss in India
line_items.source: NABCONS study for MoFPI (2022), Table 6.5 (https://www.mofpi.gov.in/sites/default/files/study_report_of_post_harvest_losses.pdf)
line_items.note: Tapioca 4.87%, mushroom 7.2%, cabbage 8.15%, tomato 11.61%. Market-level loss (transport, wholesale, retail) is 1-3.3%. The study does not cover leafy greens.

risks: One on-demand drop from a farm on the edge of the city costs ₹170-400 on the Borzo tariff. The ₹99 delivery fee loses money unless B2C orders go in routes of 15 or more drops.
The EV three-wheeler's certified range is 80 km. A farm-city-farm HoReCa loop can go past that in traffic or rain.
Quick-commerce and modern-retail margins, fees and payment days are not public. The planning assumptions (45-65% of shelf price, 30-45 days, 3-15% rejection) can be wrong.

Quick commerce needs a GSTIN, a trademark filing, FSSAI, GS1 barcodes and, for Blinkit, IRN e-invoicing and a DSC. The first order is unlikely before December 2026, and year-1 paperwork costs about ₹55-65k.
A Hyperpure bid locks the price. Delays, shortfalls and QC failures get penalties. The farm carries the delivery cost and waits for payment on credit.
The cold chain runs on grid power only. A BESCOM outage can warm the cold room, and greens lose shelf life fast when warm (mustard microgreens last 14 days at 5 °C and 1 day at 20 °C).
FSSAI may treat sales on the farm's own website as 'E-Commerce', which needs a ₹7,500 Central licence. Get written advice.
Packaging MOQs (1,000-16,000 units) and crates lost at buyers tie up cash. Printed packs lock in the SKUs too early.
Delivery services can add 18% GST. A farm that sells only exempt produce cannot claim it back.
Monsoon rain slows two-wheeler routes and wets cartons, so waterproof insulated bags are necessary.

Some sources could not be read: IndiaMART (HTTP 429), Blinkit seller pages (403), Swiggy (bot check), the Karnataka legal-metrology site and Namdhari's Fresh (no public data). Their figures come from the repo docs or are estimates.
recommendations: Sell B2C only on fixed delivery days in 1-2 dense clusters. Put 15 or more drops in each route. Each week, compare the ₹99 fee with the real cost per drop.

For the first 3 months, hire delivery instead of buying vehicles: Borzo multi-drop loops for B2C and a Porter three-wheeler for HoReCa. Buy an EV three-wheeler only when HoReCa volume is above about 100 kg/day.

Start cold storage with a used chest freezer, or a convertible one that runs as a cooler (₹12-35k). Install a walk-in cold room of 8×8×8 ft (about ₹2.6 lakh) before the harvest reaches about 100 kg/day.
Harvest at dawn. Dunk greens in ice water, spin them dry and pack them at 2-4 °C. Keep basil at 12-15 °C. Use insulated rider bags, and add gel packs only for trips longer than 2 h.

For HoReCa, use liner bags in crates (₹2-8/kg). For 100-250 g retail packs, use pouches (₹15-20/kg). Use clamshells (about ₹7 each) only for premium mixes and microgreens. Buy stock labels and a ₹13k thermal printer instead of printed packs.

Do the paperwork in this order: Udyam (free), FSSAI registration (₹100; confirm the category), GSTIN (free), trademark TM-A (₹4,500), then the Hyperpure application. Buy GS1 barcodes (₹50,200) only after a quick-commerce buyer commits in writing.
Treat quick commerce as extra income from month 3 at the earliest. Before you supply, get a written term sheet that states the margin, the payment days, and the rejection and return rules.
Record wastage by channel every week, with photos on arrival. Target 4% or less for own B2C and 5% or less for HoReCa.

topic: Fresh-produce export from Bengaluru (BLR) to the UAE and GCC for Floruvi hydroponic herbs and leafy greens: steps, costs, prices, timeline, payment risk, merchant export, and a 90-day pilot (checked 29 Sep 2026)
summary: A new exporter can legally ship fresh herbs from BLR to the UAE within 90 days. The steps are: IEC Rs 500, APEDA RCMC Rs 5,900 for 5 years, FSSAI Central licence Rs 7,500 a year, one-time PQMS registration, and one phytosanitary certificate per shipment. The UAE importer holds the import permit. The bottleneck is a verified buyer and steady farm volume, not paperwork. The first paid shipment is likely about 75 days away (range 35–150 days), so it will not meet the December 2026 cash goal. Air-freighted premium herbs from Kenya, the Netherlands and Thailand land in the GCC at USD 4.5–7.6/kg CIF, but Indian vegetables land at only USD 1.2–1.6/kg (UN Comtrade 2023–24). Floruvi basil would land in Dubai at about Rs 580/kg (USD 6.0) in a 200 kg lot, which is −Rs 150 to +Rs 150/kg compared with selling it in Bengaluru at Rs 250/kg. Do not air-freight hydroponic mint or coriander: logistics alone costs about Rs 290/kg, and their benchmark price is Rs 115–150/kg. Do not air-freight lettuce either: it loses Rs 30–190/kg. Merchant export of commodity produce pays thin margins (estimate Rs 0–20/kg) and can lock up Rs 1.5–15 lakh if buyers get credit. Recommendation: export only after the domestic farm is stable (earliest Q2 2027). In the next 90 days, finish the registrations (about Rs 14,000) and run at most one or two 50–100 kg pilots, paid 100% in advance, at USD 6.5–7/kg CPT Dubai or more.

risks: No verified buyer yet. Directory and website export leads are mostly price-only enquiries.
An air waybill is not a document of title, so documents-against-payment does not protect air shipments. Only an advance payment or a letter of credit protects the exporter.
Arrival quality claims are routine for perishables. RBI lets banks approve invoice cuts of up to 25%. Buyers can use claims to cut the price.
Bulky leaves pay for volume weight. Freight per sellable kg can be 1.5–3 times the rate per kg.
Airlines can offload belly cargo or delay it. Temperature abuse damages herbs; basil gets chilling injury below about 10 °C.
Residue or microbial failure at the border can cause rejection. Sudden sanitary bans have happened, for example the GCC bans on Kerala produce during the 2018 Nipah outbreak.
Strong competition: UAE-grown herbs fill local shelves (17 of 20 Talabat UAE herb items). Kenya, the Netherlands, Thailand and Jordan already supply premium and cheap segments.
Scale mismatch: export needs the same volume every week. The 600-tower farm will not have steady output before about Q1–Q2 2027.
Capital squeeze: Rs 20 lakh minus about Rs 4.4 lakh of fixed commitments. Buyer credit or consignment terms can lock up Rs 8–15 lakh.

Fraud red flags: a buyer asks you to pay for 'registration', an 'import permit', 'samples' or 'lab fees'; a prepaid first order is followed by large orders on credit; the company has no verifiable trade licence, uses a free email address, or has a mismatched address; unknown-bank LCs or 'SBLC/MT760' offers; an email says the bank account has changed; the buyer asks to ship to a third party or on consignment.

Regulatory gaps: the MOCCAE import-permit page blocked access ('Request Rejected'). ZAD could not be verified (zad.gov.ae refused connection). The phytosanitary fee units are not labelled. Saudi Arabia needs a Certificate of Conformity. Arabic stickers must be approved and applied before export.

Data limits: HS 070999 mixes many products. The latest UAE import data are from 2023. Air freight, terminal, packaging and wholesale figures are estimates. The web search budget ran out, so this work used direct page fetches only.

B2C export of fresh produce is not practical, because each consignment needs a phytosanitary certificate and an importer's permit. The website's export versions can create orders that cannot be filled.
recommendations: Decision: do not count on export for the 3-month cash goal. Sell the first harvests in Bengaluru (B2B and B2C). Scale export after 8–12 weeks of stable farm output, at the earliest in Q2 2027.
Step 1: Get the IEC (Rs 500). Open the current account and register the AD code with customs at the BLR air cargo complex.
Step 2: Apply for the APEDA RCMC on the DGFT portal (Rs 5,900 for 5 years).
Step 3: Register once as an exporter on PQMS.
Step 4: Apply for the FSSAI Central licence as Trader/Merchant – Exporter (Rs 7,500 a year). Ask a CA to confirm this category for a grower-exporter.
Step 5: Get written quotes from 2–3 forwarders for FCA BLR and CPT Dubai. Ask for the rate per chargeable kg, minimum charges, cold-room, AWB, screening and CHA fees.
Step 6: Test one crop batch at a NABL lab before you offer it (IIHR residue test Rs 5,900–11,800, plus microbial tests). Check APEDA and KAPPEC support first.

Step 7: Check each importer before you ship: UAE trade licence, food-import registration, ability to get the MOCCAE permit for each consignment, and 2 trade references. Ask which platform they use (for example ZAD).

Pilot rule: send only premium items (Italian or Thai basil, cut microgreens, edible flowers) in 50–100 kg lots. Quote at least USD 6.5–7/kg CPT Dubai (AED 24–26/kg). A 100 kg shipment needs about Rs 33,000 of logistics cash.
Payment rule: take 100% advance by bank transfer for the first 3–5 shipments. Do not sell on D/P, D/A, open account, consignment or auction terms.
Do not export mint, coriander or lettuce by air. They lose Rs 30–240/kg against import benchmarks.

Merchant export: do only back-to-back deals where the buyer pays in advance, or sell to an established BLR exporter in India. The fastest known lines are green chillies and Indian vegetables to the UAE; margins are thin (Rs 0–20/kg).
Buy ECGC Small Exporters Policy cover (minimum premium Rs 5,000) and set buyer limits before you give any credit.
Keep a price rule: every export quote must include freight on chargeable weight, fixed shipment costs spread over the lot, and a 10% shrink allowance.
Treat the website's 16 export versions as B2B quote requests only. Do not accept consumer export orders for fresh produce.

For docs/22 section 6: the RCMC fee (Rs 5,900 for 5 years) and the FSSAI exporter licence (Rs 7,500) are now verified. UAE documents (invoice, chamber CoO, packing list, AWB, original health or phytosanitary certificate) and Arabic labelling are confirmed by trade.gov. MOCCAE permit details and ZAD are still not verified. No GCC pack-house rule was found; APEDA lists special pack-house and residue procedures only for certain products bound for the EU.

topic: Subsidies, finance, legal and tax rules, and failure modes for a 600-tower hydroponic farm near Bengaluru (Floruvi), checked 29 Sep 2026
summary: No subsidy will pay you cash in the first 3 months. Every capital subsidy needs approval before you build and pays only after inspection, usually 6 to 24 months later. The best tool is the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF). Hydroponic, vertical and polyhouse farms qualify. SBI charges 9.00% fixed, and the 3% subvention brings this to about 6% on loans up to Rs 2 crore, with up to 2 years moratorium and a CGTMSE guarantee in place of collateral. The MIDH grant limits are Rs 1.75 lakh for a hydroponics add-on, Rs 14.2 lakh for a shade net (4,000 m²) and Rs 12.5 lakh for a farm-gate pack house, but Karnataka's 2025-26 MIDH list has no polyhouse or shade-net guideline. You cannot use NHB for now: it pays 35% since 21-08-2026, needs more than 4,000 m² on one site and a 10-year title, and does not list lettuce. A normal bank loan costs 10.7-12.3% (SBI), which is about Rs 18,900-19,700 a month per Rs 10 lakh over 6 years; if you borrow to build all 600 towers, the EMI would be about Rs 1.6-1.8 lakh a month. Fresh greens are GST-exempt, so the 5-18% GST on inputs is a cost you cannot recover, and an FSSAI central licence (Rs 7,500 a year) applies to online and export sales. After the Rs 4.4 lakh commitment and a Rs 3-5 lakh reserve, only about Rs 10-12.6 lakh is safe to spend: enough for a 40-60 tower pilot, not 600 towers.

line_items.name: MIDH hydroponics/aeroponics add-on subsidy
line_items.source: MIDH Operational Guidelines April 2025, Annexure V B.5.11(i) (nhb.gov.in/writereaddata/MIDH_Guidelines.pdf)
line_items.note: Norm Rs 350/m2, 50%, max 1,000 m2. Only as an add-on inside a polyhouse or shade net. You need a work order before you build; it pays after inspection, never within 3 months. Karnataka's 2025-26 MIDH guidelines do not list it, so base is 0.

line_items.name: MIDH shade-net house subsidy (tubular)
line_items.source: MIDH Operational Guidelines April 2025, Annexure V B.5.2(a); MoA&FW letter M-14011/5/2024-MIDH dated 12-08-2025 (4,000 m2 limit)
line_items.note: Rs 710/m2 x 50% x max 4,000 m2. The 60-cent plot alone (2,428 m2) caps at Rs 8.6 lakh. A naturally ventilated polyhouse (Rs 1,200 to 950/m2 slabs) caps at about Rs 20.1 lakh for 4,000 m2. You need selection and a work order before you build. It pays in instalments after joint inspections, you must use the structure for 10 years, and insurance is mandatory (Telangana example). Karnataka has posted no 2025-26 guideline for it, so base is 0 within 12 months.

line_items.name: MIDH farm-gate pack house + farm-gate cold store subsidy
line_items.source: Karnataka Dept of Horticulture MIDH 2025-26 PHM guideline (horticulturedir.karnataka.gov.in/uploads/media_to_upload1758700999.pdf); MIDH Annexure V C.1
line_items.note: Unit cost up to Rs 25 lakh (9 x 6 m), 50%. Components include a grid cold room (Rs 5 lakh norm). You need a FRUITS farmer ID (FID), a current RTC with the crop entered, and a work order through HASIRU before you build. It pays after inspection, in 6-12+ months (estimate).

line_items.name: Karnataka MIDH small add-ons: weed mat + individual farm pond
line_items.source: Karnataka MIDH 2025-26 guidelines: weed mat (media_to_upload1758706503.pdf), farm pond (media_to_upload1758699345.pdf)
line_items.note: Weed mat: Rs 50/m2 norm, 50% = Rs 25/m2, max Rs 1.0 lakh. Farm pond: max Rs 0.75 lakh (minimum 300 m3). Get the work order first. These are 2025-26 guidelines, so confirm the 2026-27 targets.

line_items.name: NHB protected-cultivation subsidy (Scheme 1)
line_items.source: NHB Public Circular NHB/CC/Guidelines/2026-27/2101 dated 21-08-2026; NHB Operational Guideline Jan 2025; NHB LoC/GoC instructions (rev. 31-08-2023)
line_items.note: 35% of eligible cost (was 50%). Needs more than 4,000 m2 per beneficiary. The only vegetables listed are capsicum, cucumber and tomato (not lettuce). Ceilings are Rs 55 lakh/acre for a polyhouse and Rs 40 lakh/acre for a shade net. You need the NHB clearance letter (GoC) before any work, and the bank must not release the loan before it. Complete within 18 months and claim within 21 months of the first loan instalment. If the loan turns non-performing (NPA), NHB recovers the subsidy with interest. You cannot take NHB and MIDH for the same project. Both of your plots are too small, so base is 0.

line_items.name: NHB and NHM minimum protected area per beneficiary
line_items.source: MoA&FW (MIDH) letter dated 12-08-2025; NHB Operational Guideline Jan 2025 ('areas exceeding 4000 sq m')
line_items.note: NHB needs 4,000 m2 or more; the state NHM caps protected cultivation at 4,000 m2. Your plots are 2,428 m2 and 1,619 m2, on separate sites.

line_items.name: Land tenure needed for NHB/MIDH-assisted assets
line_items.unit: years of title, registered lease or mandatory use
line_items.source: NHB instructions for LoC/GoC item 4; Telangana MIDH Implementation Guidelines 2025-26 (10-year use)
line_items.note: The 1-year rent-free plot cannot carry subsidised assets.

line_items.name: AIF interest subvention
line_items.source: AIF Revised Scheme Guidelines Sept 2024; AIF FAQ (agriinfra.dac.gov.in)
line_items.note: On loans up to Rs 2 crore, for max 7 years. Hydroponic, vertical and aeroponic farming and polyhouses are listed as eligible, also for individual farmers. No capital subsidy, and working capital is not eligible. Minimum 10% own contribution (a capital subsidy counts toward it). The sanction target is 60 days or less. The fund was still sanctioning in June-Aug 2026, but about 95% of the Rs 1 lakh crore was already sanctioned. NABARD refinances the lenders.

line_items.name: AIF effective borrower interest rate
line_items.source: SBI Agriculture Segment Interest Structure as on 15-09-2026 (AIF loan: 9.00% fixed up to Rs 2 crore); AIF FAQ (9% cap on rate of interest)
line_items.note: Base = 9.00% minus the 3% subvention. Low: estimate, if a bank prices below the cap. High: if you pay the full rate until the subvention is credited.

line_items.name: Non-AIF bank term loan rate (polyhouse/horticulture)
line_items.source: SBI Agriculture Segment Interest Structure 15-09-2026; SBI MCLR w.e.f. 15-09-2026 (1-year 8.70%); RBI policy repo 5.25%
line_items.note: SBI poly-house loan under Rs 50 lakh = 1-year MCLR + 2.00%. Other farm and horticulture term loans = 1-year MCLR + 3.60%. At Rs 50 lakh or more, the rate depends on your credit rating. Banks usually want a debt-service cover ratio (DSCR) of about 1.25-1.5 (estimate).

line_items.name: EMI per Rs 10 lakh borrowed (72 months after moratorium)
line_items.source: Computed at 6%, 10.7% and 12.3% p.a.
line_items.note: Also add interest during the moratorium: Rs 60,000 to 1,23,000 per Rs 10 lakh per year.

line_items.name: EMI if 600 towers are 90% loan-funded
line_items.source: Computed from team capex estimate for 600 towers incl. ancillaries (Rs 68.5 / 104.8 / 165.5 lakh), 90% loan, 72 months; 6% (low, base) and 10.7% (high)
line_items.note: Also Rs 3.7-8.9 lakh of interest for each year of moratorium. This comes on top of the existing Rs 40,000/month commitment.

line_items.name: Loan moratorium available
line_items.source: AIF FAQ (repayment 7 years incl. 6-24 months moratorium); Stand-Up India (max 18 months)
line_items.note: NHB requires you to finish the project within 18 months (+6) of the first loan instalment.

line_items.name: Own contribution (margin) on project loans
line_items.source: AIF guidelines s.13 (minimum 10%); Stand-Up India (25%, of which 15% can come from schemes, minimum 10% own money); base = estimate for typical farm term loans
line_items.note: The base figure is an estimate. Each bank decides.

line_items.name: AIF credit guarantee (CGTMSE, fee paid by Government)
line_items.source: AIF Revised Scheme Guidelines Sept 2024 s.5; AIF FAQ Q17
line_items.note: The FAQ says no collateral is needed up to Rs 2 crore, but branches may still ask. Outside AIF, expect the bank to ask for a mortgage on your owned land.

line_items.name: KCC crop-loan interest
line_items.source: SBI Agriculture Segment Interest Structure 15-09-2026 (7% up to Rs 3 lakh; 1-year MCLR + 3.25% above)
line_items.note: The 4% low assumes the 3% prompt-repayment incentive (not checked again today). You need a FRUITS farmer ID and an RTC with the crop entered. Farm loans up to Rs 2 lakh need no collateral (RBI; not checked again today). A KCC is fast: weeks, not months.

line_items.name: MUDRA loan for Floruvi retail/packing/delivery arm
line_items.source: mudra.org.in Offerings page (updated 25-09-2026)
line_items.note: For non-farm micro businesses. Crop loans are excluded, so it cannot pay for growing. The Rs 20 lakh level (Tarun Plus) is only for people who have repaid a Tarun loan. No collateral (CGFMU guarantee). It is a loan, not a grant.

line_items.name: Stand-Up India loan
line_items.source: standupmitra.in (Stand-Up India scheme page)
line_items.note: Rs 10 lakh to 1 crore, for new businesses only, and only for SC/ST and/or women holding 51%. 7 years, up to 18 months moratorium, at least 10% own money, rate capped at MCLR + 3% + tenor premium. Base is 0 unless you or a woman partner qualifies.

line_items.name: PMEGP margin-money subsidy
line_items.source: PMEGP guidelines (KVIC); kviconline.gov.in did not resolve on 29-09-2026, so not checked again today
line_items.note: Last known rules: projects up to Rs 50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 20 lakh (service); subsidy 15-25% for general and 25-35% for special categories. Crop cultivation and horticulture are on the negative list. The bank holds the subsidy as a 3-year term deposit, so there is no cash in 3, 6 or 12 months.

line_items.name: PMFME capital subsidy (processing only)
line_items.source: PMFME scheme (pmfme.mofpi.gov.in; details not checked again today); SBI lists a PMFME term-loan product on 15-09-2026
line_items.note: Last known rules: 35% of cost, linked to a bank loan, max Rs 10 lakh per micro food-processing unit (for example dried herbs or cut salads). It does not cover growing. It pays after the unit is built, which takes months.

line_items.name: NHB application (LoC/GoC) fee
line_items.source: NHB Public Circular dated 21-08-2026, item 7
line_items.note: Rs 2,000 (project up to Rs 20 lakh), Rs 5,000 (Rs 20-50 lakh), Rs 10,000 (Rs 50-100 lakh), plus GST.

line_items.name: Detailed project report (DPR) for bank/AIF
line_items.source: IndiaFilings business-plan page (bank-loan plan Rs 10,000-30,000 + GST); AIF FAQ (you may write your own DPR from the model template)
line_items.note: Low = you write it yourself from the AIF model DPR.

line_items.name: CA, bookkeeping and tax filing
line_items.source: IndiaFilings pricing (ITR from Rs 2,899 + GST a year; GST filing + ITR with a dedicated accountant Rs 19,899 + GST a year, turnover up to Rs 40 lakh); high = estimate for a local CA doing monthly books
line_items.note: Also budget for CA expenditure certificates for loan or subsidy claims (estimate Rs 3,000-15,000 each).

line_items.name: FSSAI licence/registration
line_items.source: FSSAI FoSCoS 'Kind of Business' eligibility criteria (updated 01-04-2026); IndiaFilings FSSAI page (agent fee Rs 1,899 + GST)
line_items.note: A retailer with turnover up to Rs 1.5 crore needs only registration (Rs 100). E-commerce and trader-exporter businesses need a central licence (Rs 7,500) at any turnover. A farmer who sells own produce at the farm is outside licensing (legal view).

line_items.name: APEDA RCMC (export registration)
line_items.source: APEDA circular on e-RCMC dated 21-07-2023 (issued via DGFT portal)
line_items.note: You need the IEC first. For fresh fruit and vegetables, proof can be an FSSAI, Udyam or Horticulture Dept certificate.

line_items.name: GST on sales of fresh leafy greens
line_items.source: CBIC GST rate schedule (HSN 0704, 0705 lettuce, 0709 fresh = Nil); fresh vegetables not in the 56th GST Council (Sept 2025) rate changes
line_items.note: A seller of exempt goods only need not register and cannot claim input tax credit, so all input GST is a cost. Exports under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) are zero-rated and may allow input-GST refunds if you register (IGST Act s.16; confirm with a CA).

line_items.name: Non-recoverable GST on farm inputs
line_items.source: 56th GST Council recommendations (effective 22-09-2025), gstcouncil.gov.in
line_items.note: 5%: drip and sprinklers, horticultural machinery incl. germination plant, bio-pesticides incl. neem, micronutrients, fertiliser acids. 18% (estimate): plastic towers and pipes, electricals, CCTV; these are not in the cut list. Record capex including GST.

line_items.name: Income tax on hydroponic profit (individual, marginal rate)
line_items.source: Income-tax Act 2025, s.2 definition of 'agricultural income' (Bill clause 2(5), prsindia.org); Supreme Court test in CIT v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy (1957)
line_items.note: Soilless produce may not count as 'agricultural income': the law deems only nursery saplings and seedlings to be agricultural. Plan for business-income tax. Base 0 assumes your total income stays within the new-regime rebate (Rs 12 lakh in FY2025-26; check FY2026-27). High = 30% + 4% cess. I found no court ruling on hydroponics.

line_items.name: Asset insurance: fire, STFI (storm, tempest, flood, inundation) and burglary
line_items.unit: % of sum insured per year incl. GST
line_items.source: estimate: no public tariff found; typical small-business package pricing; get 3 quotes
line_items.note: NHB requires project insurance wherever cover exists. Telangana MIDH requires polyhouse insurance before the first subsidy instalment.

line_items.name: Polyhouse/shade-net structure and film cover
line_items.source: estimate: covers for farm structures carry storm and film risk, so they cost more than fire cover; no public rate found
line_items.note: Policies often exclude film tears or carry high deductibles. Read the policy wording.

line_items.name: Crop insurance for hydroponic greens
line_items.source: estimate: PMFBY covers notified crops only; the farmer share for commercial and horticultural crops is 5%
line_items.note: Assume no cover exists. You carry crop losses yourself, so spread risk across many small systems.

line_items.name: Power supply on agricultural (IP-set) feeders
line_items.source: KERC Combined ESCOMs Tariff Order 2025 (BESCOM: IP sets get only 6-7 hours per Government Order; ESCOMs regulate hours on agricultural feeders)
line_items.note: Hydroponic pumps need power 24x7. The BESCOM tariff lists 'Green House' under LT-5: Rs 4.40/kWh + Rs 150/HP/month in FY2026-27, with a 20 paise rebate in village panchayat areas. Farm-pump (LT-4) power used for other purposes is billed at the LT-3/LT-5 rate.

line_items.name: Crop loss from a root-disease outbreak (per affected system)
line_items.unit: % of plants on the affected reservoir
line_items.source: University of Kentucky CCD-CP-63 Hydroponic Lettuce (complete loss possible; no registered fungicides); low and base = estimate
line_items.note: Cornell CEA handbook: keep the solution at 25 C or below; dissolved oxygen under 3 ppm means crop failure. Many small independent reservoirs limit the damage.

line_items.name: Deployable capital after commitments and reserve
line_items.source: Computed: Rs 20 lakh - Rs 4.4 lakh (11 x Rs 40,000 to Aug 2027) - reserve of Rs 7.6 / 5 / 3 lakh
line_items.note: At the team's base capex (about Rs 14,000 per installed tower plus site costs), this pays for about 40-60 towers, not 600.

line_items.name: Time from application to subsidy cash: MIDH/NHM (state)
line_items.source: estimate from the Karnataka MIDH 2025-26 process (FRUITS/HASIRU selection within district targets, work order, build, inspection) and the Telangana 2-instalment inspection rule
line_items.note: It cannot pay within 3 months.

line_items.name: Time from application to subsidy cash: NHB
line_items.source: NHB Office Order dated 06-05-2026 (clearance within 30 days; claim processing timelines); NHB LoC/GoC instructions (completion within 18 months, claim within 21 months)
line_items.note: The low figure assumes a fast build and a clean joint inspection.

line_items.name: AIF loan sanction time
line_items.source: AIF FAQ Q21 (60 days or less if everything goes smoothly); low and high = estimate
line_items.note: It is a loan, not a grant. The subvention goes through the bank.

risks: No buyers or oversupply: 600 towers (about 54,000 sites) would produce roughly 100-140 kg of leafy greens a day (team yield model). Wholesale pays about 25-40% of retail per plant and restaurants (HoReCa) about 30-65% (team price model). Evidence: Bowery Farming shut in Nov 2024 after weak demand for high-priced greens and a pathogen outbreak (PitchBook, via Wikipedia). AeroFarms (June 2023) and AppHarvest (July 2023) filed for Chapter 11. Mitigation: pre-sell standing orders, add towers only against confirmed demand, and use Floruvi B2C boxes and microgreens.

Power cuts: the KERC Tariff Order 2025 records BESCOM stating that IP-set (farm pump) feeders get only 6-7 hours of supply a day by Government Order, and ESCOMs ration hours on farm feeders by subsidy release. Tower and NFT roots dry quickly when pumps stop. Mitigation: an LT-5 'Green House' connection on a 24x7 feeder, inverter/battery for pumps, a generator, a header tank and power-fail alarms.

Root disease and heat: University of Kentucky says water moulds (Pythium, Phytophthora) spread through recirculating systems, no fungicide is registered for greenhouse lettuce, and complete crop loss can follow. Cornell sets the solution at 25 C or below and warns that dissolved oxygen under 3 ppm means crop failure. Bengaluru's April-May highs reach about 34-35 C (IMD normals; team climate notes from UAS-GKVK). Mitigation: many small independent reservoirs, shade, insulated or chilled tanks, sanitation, seedling quarantine.

Debt and cash gap: capital subsidies pay after the work is done, 6-24 months later, while you already owe Rs 40,000 a month until Aug 2027. A 600-tower build (about Rs 1.05 crore base, team capex) at 90% debt needs about Rs 1.56 lakh a month EMI even at the AIF rate of about 6% (Rs 1.78 lakh at 10.7%), plus moratorium interest. NHB takes back the subsidy with interest if the loan turns NPA. Mitigation: fund the pilot with your own cash, and borrow only via AIF after 2-3 profitable cycles.

Vendor over-selling: your tower quotes (Rs 5,000-12,000) are below the team's installed-cost estimate (about Rs 10,000-21,000 per tower), so cheap quotes may leave out pumps, tanks, structure or UV-stable plastic. NHB states it is not responsible for faults by technology or service providers. Telangana MIDH makes the farmer liable for structure damage. Mitigation: trial 5-10 towers, see reference farms, get written specs and a warranty, and refuse buy-back or guaranteed-income offers.

Labour and owner absence: hydroponics needs daily checks of EC, pH and dissolved oxygen (University of Kentucky advises daily inspection), and one pump or dosing fault can kill a crop in hours. Mitigation: be on site daily for the first 6 months, hire one trained grower plus helpers, and use written procedures, sensors with alarms, CCTV and a night watchman.

Subsidy and policy changes: NHB cut protected-cultivation subsidy from 50% to 35% on 21-08-2026 and added a once-per-family rule. The minimum protected area moved from 2,500 to 4,000 m2 (12-08-2025). Karnataka's 2025-26 MIDH list has no polyhouse or shade-net guideline. AIF had about 95% of its Rs 1 lakh crore sanctioned by mid-2026 and may close. Mitigation: make the business case work with zero subsidy.

Land and collateral: the large plot is rent-free for 1 year only, but NHB needs owned or registered-lease land for 10 years or more, and MIDH structures must stay in use for 10 years. Outside AIF (CGTMSE cover), banks will ask to mortgage your owned 1 acre for a Rs 30-60 lakh loan, so a failure could cost the family land.

Tax and legal classification: the Income-tax Act 2025 counts income as agricultural only if it comes from land by agriculture (plus nursery saplings and seedlings), so tower produce may be taxed as business income; I verified no court ruling on hydroponics. Running the farm on a cheap farm-pump (IP-set) connection gets it billed at LT-3/LT-5 rates. False or hidden facts in subsidy declarations lead to recovery with interest.
Export timing: fresh-greens export needs an FSSAI central licence, APEDA RCMC after IEC, phytosanitary certificates and cold-chain air freight. Export will not produce cash within 3 months.
Owner stress and burnout: a crop system that runs 24x7, plus debt and family expectations, can push you to make rushed decisions. Mitigation: grow in phases, keep a cash reserve, and share the work.
recommendations: Do not build 600 towers now. Start with a pilot you can pay for from safe cash (about Rs 10-12.6 lakh, roughly 40-60 installed towers at the team's base capex) on the owned 60-cent plot. Add towers only after two cycles of paid, repeat orders.
Keep Rs 4.4 lakh aside for the Rs 40,000/month commitment to Aug 2027, and hold a Rs 3-5 lakh operating reserve. Do not spend either on towers.

Count every subsidy as a bonus, never as cash flow. No scheme pays within 3 months. MIDH, NHB, PMEGP and PMFME all need approval (work order, GoC or sanction) before you build, and work you start earlier is not eligible.

If you borrow, use the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF): hydroponics qualifies, SBI charges 9.00% fixed (about 6% after the 3% subvention), repayment is 7 years with up to 2 years moratorium, and CGTMSE covers loans up to Rs 2 crore. Avoid personal loans, credit cards, gold loans and private lenders.
Register on the FRUITS portal, update the RTC crop entry and open a KCC for working capital (SBI: 7% up to Rs 3 lakh). Every Karnataka horticulture subsidy needs the FRUITS ID and RTC.

Before you build, apply at the Horticulture office for the 2026-27 MIDH items that fit: weed mat (up to Rs 1 lakh), farm pond (up to Rs 0.75 lakh) and farm-gate pack house/cold room (50%, up to Rs 12.5 lakh). Ask whether shade-net or hydroponics add-on targets exist. Build only after you get the work order.
Skip NHB for now. It needs more than 4,000 m2 on one site and a 10-year title or registered lease, pays 35%, lists capsicum, cucumber and tomato (not lettuce), and pays 12-24 months later.
Get an LT-5 ('Green House') connection on a 24x7 feeder, never an IP-set (farm pump) feeder. Budget for battery backup for pumps, a generator, a header tank and power-fail alarms.
Design against disease: split towers into many small independent reservoirs, shade the crop, keep the solution at or below 25 C, sanitise between cycles and quarantine new seedlings.
Sell before you grow. Sign standing orders with cafes, restaurants and cloud kitchens, and use Floruvi B2C boxes and microgreens for early cash. Do not plan on export income in the first 3 months.

Compliance: get an FSSAI central licence (Rs 7,500/year) because you sell online and plan exports. Get APEDA RCMC (Rs 5,900 for 5 years) after the IEC, and a free Udyam registration for the trading arm. You need no GST registration for exempt produce unless you export under a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) to reclaim input GST; ask a CA.
Get a written CA opinion on agricultural vs business income, and keep full books from day one.

Land and water: growing should not need land conversion (legal view; confirm with the Tahsildar). A pack house needs local-body building permission. Check Karnataka Ground Water Authority rules before you drill a new borewell, because Bengaluru taluks are over-exploited (CGWB).
Insure structures and equipment against fire, storm/flood and burglary (estimate 0.15-0.6% of value a year; get 3 quotes). No crop insurance exists for hydroponic greens.

Buy 5-10 towers first and test them for 1-2 cycles. Ask for reference farms, food-grade UV-stable plastic, pump specifications and a written warranty. Refuse buy-back or guaranteed-income offers. Put no fixed assets on the 1-year rent-free land.

Take no shortcuts. If you run the farm on a free IP-set connection or give wrong subsidy declarations, you will face back-billing and recovery with interest. For night security, hire a watchman directly or use a PSARA-licensed agency.
Keep the plan survivable: grow in phases, keep the reserve and share the work. If stress or low mood lasts, Tele-MANAS (14416) gives free support 24x7.
